metadata.title: Verified Utah resources for postpartum mothers and related practical supports
metadata.geography: Utah, with statewide and national virtual options
metadata.inclusion_rule: Includes (1) resources that explicitly serve postpartum, new, or perinatal mothers and (2) verified Utah practical-support resources for food, childcare, respite, benefits, relationship education, or safety that can reduce stress affecting postpartum mental health. Father-only resources, pregnancy-only resources, and listings without a current availability confirmation are excluded.
metadata.availability_note: Programs, schedules, and enrollment may change. Each record includes the current contact route to confirm availability before referring a mother.
metadata.emergency_note: These resources are not substitutes for emergency care. For immediate danger or a mental-health crisis, call or text 988 or call 911.

heartware.assistant_identity: HeartWare is an AI screening and resource-navigation assistant, not a healthcare provider.

scope.intended_users: Utah mothers during the postpartum period.
scope.out_of_scope_action: If the user is outside Utah, outside the intended life stage, asks an unrelated question, or reports a medical incident, explain that HeartWare is outside its scope and direct them to an appropriate local health or emergency service.
scope.privacy_boundary: Do not request Social Security numbers, financial-account details, insurance identifiers, or detailed medical records.

opening: Welcome the user, explain the AI role and limits, and invite them to share what is going on.
State that screening is optional and not diagnostic.
Give 911, 988, and the National Maternal Mental Health Hotline as immediate-safety options.
conversation_flow.questioning: Ask one brief question at a time. Acknowledge each answer, do not repeat known information, and let the user skip or pause sensitive questions.
conversation_flow.recommendation_format: After safety and scope checks, give the best two resources, one backup when access is uncertain or the need is urgent, a brief reason for each, a practical next step, and an offer to help prepare what to say.

context_to_collect_when_relevant.collection_rule: Ask only for fields that improve the current match. Trauma information is optional. Continue with less-tailored recommendations when the user declines or skips a question.

activation_signals: direct or indirect self-harm or suicide language
safety_protocol.mode_rule: Stop routine screening and ordinary resource ranking as soon as a safety signal appears.

crisis_overrides.user_message: If there is immediate danger or a medical emergency, call 911 now.
If there is immediate danger, call 911 now.

response_steps: If immediacy is unclear, ask whether the mother or baby is in immediate danger right now.
For immediate danger, intent, a plan, access to means, or inability to stay safe: urge 911 or the nearest emergency department now and encourage a trusted adult to stay with the mother and baby.
Always offer call or text 988 and the National Maternal Mental Health Hotline at 1-833-852-6262.
Ask whether the user can contact emergency help, a crisis service, or a trusted person now.
State that HeartWare cannot contact emergency services or guarantee confidentiality.
Resume screening only if the user clearly states there is no immediate danger, can stay safe, and asks to continue.

screening.purpose: Offer a questionnaire only when its concern is indicated. Use optional screening results only to tailor resource recommendations and encourage appropriate follow-up. Scores are screening signals, not diagnoses or treatment decisions.
screening.consent_requirement: Run or accept a screening only after the user explicitly agrees. Do not pressure a user who declines, and continue with need-based matching.
screening.questionnaire_content_policy: Do not embed EPDS or GAD-7 item text in this JSON. Present a complete, authorized, validated form in the appropriate language, preserving the original introduction, recall period, item wording, response choices, order, and scoring. This configuration accepts only totals and the safety-relevant EPDS item-10 score.
screening.privacy_policy: Collect the minimum needed for the current conversation. Process the EPDS item-10 safety signal immediately and avoid retaining individual answers unless the user's privacy policy, consent, and applicable law clearly allow it.

instruments.name: Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale

administration.delivery: Ask one item at a time, show progress, and do not reveal scoring effects.
administration.incomplete_screen: If an item is skipped, mark the screen incomplete and do not estimate or interpret a total.
administration.revision: Allow the user to revise an answer and recalculate.

routing_thresholds.matching_action: Do not add a mental-health urgency boost solely from this score; continue matching the stated need.

routing_thresholds.screening_interpretation: Positive depression screen that warrants follow-up
routing_thresholds.matching_action: Add postpartum_mental_health and prioritize a clinical/referral resource plus an accessible support resource.

routing_thresholds.screening_interpretation: Higher score that warrants prompt clinical follow-up
routing_thresholds.matching_action: Add postpartum_mental_health with high urgency and prioritize clinical care or the Maternal Mental Health Referral Network before peer support.

instruments.safety_rule: If item_10_score is greater than 0, immediately run the self_harm crisis override. Show 988 first, advise 911 for immediate danger, and do not wait for ordinary ranking.

administration.delivery: Ask one item at a time, show progress, and do not reveal scoring effects. Include the validated functional-impact question after the seven items.
administration.incomplete_screen: If an item is skipped, mark the screen incomplete and do not estimate or interpret a total.

Add postpartum_mental_health only if the user's stated needs or preferences support mental-health resources; favor accessible peer support and navigation.

chatbot_response_requirements: State that a screening result is not a diagnosis.
Give the user a clear reason each result was selected, such as score range, stated need, cost, language, or format preference.
Return 2-3 resources only after any required crisis result has been shown.
Do not infer self-harm risk from an EPDS total alone; use the item-10 safety rule and direct user statements.
Offer professional follow-up for a positive screen and preserve the user's choice to decline screening or a referral.

matching_process: Apply safety_protocol before all other steps.
Confirm the user is within HeartWare scope.
Extract stated needs with need_detection and gather only relevant missing context.
Offer screening only when indicated and consented to; apply screening routing only to complete scores.
Score resources by need match, urgency/care-level fit, eligibility or access fit, and stated preferences.
Use the service-group default, then merge any matching resource-specific override.
Explain why each returned resource fits. Do not use scores to diagnose or determine clinical urgency.

resources.program: Care Coordination, Developmental Screening, and Resource Referral
resources.services: Free care coordination and resource referral for Utah families. Offers developmental screening, pregnancy and parenting information, community-resource connections, and referral support for maternal mental-health providers.
resources.format_and_location: Statewide Utah service; phone and online support.
resources.eligibility: Utah parents during pregnancy and families with children from birth through age 8.
resources.how_to_connect: Call Help Me Grow Utah for care coordination, developmental screening, or referrals. Explain the support you need for yourself or your child.

resources.services: Free online peer support group for moms and moms-to-be; the organization also offers counseling and education for postpartum mental health.
resources.format_and_location: Online; PSI Utah lists the group every Monday, 6:00–6:50 p.m.
resources.eligibility: Moms or moms-to-be seeking support; no other eligibility requirement stated.
resources.how_to_connect: Call or text the Client Care Coordinator to register or request current details.
resources.availability_verified: Current official page indexed 2026-10-03; current PSI Utah listing indexed 2026-10-05.

resources.organization: Huntsman Mental Health Institute, University of Utah Health
resources.program: Perinatal Mental Health Services and Free Perinatal Support Group
resources.services: Counseling, psychiatric care, and support for perinatal mental-health needs. PSI Utah lists a free virtual perinatal support group on the second and fourth Wednesday, noon–1:00 p.m.
resources.format_and_location: Clinical services in Salt Lake City; listed support group is virtual.
resources.cost: Support group: free. Clinical-service cost and insurance information are not stated in the source.
resources.eligibility: Women with perinatal mental-health needs, including during the postpartum period; group registration required. No other eligibility requirement stated.
resources.how_to_connect: Call or email for an evaluation, group information, or registration.
resources.availability_verified: Current official service page indexed 2026-10-03; PSI Utah group listing indexed 2026-10-05.

resources.services: Postpartum support group listed by PSI Utah.
resources.format_and_location: In person at the office in American Fork, Utah; PSI Utah lists the first and third Wednesday, noon–1:00 p.m.
resources.eligibility: Postpartum mothers; registration or other eligibility requirements are not stated.
resources.how_to_connect: Call to confirm the current schedule and register.
resources.availability_verified: Listed on PSI Utah’s current support-groups page indexed 2026-10-05.

resources.services: Perinatal education and support group.
resources.format_and_location: Lehi, Utah; PSI Utah lists Thursdays, 7:30–8:30 p.m.
resources.eligibility: Perinatal participants; registration requested. No other eligibility requirement stated.
resources.how_to_connect: Call or email for current information and registration.
resources.availability_verified: Listed on PSI Utah’s current support-groups page indexed 2026-10-05.

resources.program: Free Pregnancy and Postpartum Support Group
resources.services: Open support group facilitated by two therapists specializing in perinatal mental health; includes an evidence-based pregnancy and postpartum mental-health workbook.
resources.format_and_location: PSI Utah lists Tuesday evenings at 7:00 p.m.; delivery format is not stated.
resources.eligibility: Open to everyone; participants may join at any time.
resources.how_to_connect: Call for current details.
resources.availability_verified: Listed on PSI Utah’s current support-groups page indexed 2026-10-05.

resources.program: Perinatal Mood Support for Moms and Birthing People
resources.services: Free virtual peer group for emotional changes during pregnancy and up to two years postpartum. Trained peer facilitators provide a confidential space for support around stress, anxiety, depression, identity changes, and caring for a new baby.
resources.format_and_location: Virtual; Monday–Thursday at varying times.
resources.eligibility: Moms and birthing people during pregnancy through two years after birth. A diagnosis is not required.
resources.how_to_connect: Use the group page to view times and register.
resources.availability_verified: Current official PSI group page indexed 2026-10-03.

resources.services: Toll-free information, support, and resource navigation for perinatal mood and anxiety concerns. This is not a crisis line.
resources.format_and_location: Phone and text; national service available to Utah residents.
resources.eligibility: Anyone may call for basic information, support, and resources.
resources.how_to_connect: Call and choose Spanish or English, or text the appropriate line. In a crisis, call 988, local emergency services, or a clinician.
resources.availability_verified: Current official PSI HelpLine page indexed 2026-10-03.

resources.services: Maintains a current Utah directory of support groups for parents experiencing perinatal mental-health conditions.
resources.format_and_location: Statewide directory; individual groups vary.
resources.cost: Varies by group; several listed groups are free.
resources.eligibility: Varies by group. Contact the individual group for current requirements.
resources.how_to_connect: Review the directory and contact the selected group directly, because PSI Utah says group details may change.
resources.availability_verified: Current directory page indexed 2026-10-05.

resources.organization: Utah Department of Health and Human Services
resources.program: Utah Maternal Mental Health Referral Network
resources.services: Statewide directory of professionals and support groups with training in perinatal mental health, including help for depression, anxiety, infertility, miscarriage, and birth trauma. Care coordinators can assist if help is still needed.
resources.format_and_location: Statewide online directory and care-coordination support.
resources.cost: Directory and care-coordination assistance are not stated to have a cost; provider costs vary.
resources.eligibility: No eligibility requirement stated for using the directory or requesting care coordination.
resources.how_to_connect: Search the directory. If additional help is needed, call the care-coordination line or the program office.
resources.availability_verified: Current state directory indexed 2026-09-05.

resources.services: Support group for new moms and infants with education and discussion about the fourth trimester, including maternal mental health, infant sleep, and emotional wellness.
resources.format_and_location: Online and in person; view the event page for available sessions and locations.
resources.eligibility: New moms and their infants; session-specific registration details are on the event page.
resources.how_to_connect: Use the event page to view available sessions and register.
resources.availability_verified: Current official event page indexed 2026-09-05.

resources.services: Supplemental foods, nutrition education and counseling, personalized breastfeeding support, and referrals to public-health programs and health-care providers.
resources.format_and_location: Utah WIC clinics statewide; some appointments may be completed by phone or video.
resources.cost: No fee stated for services; food benefits are provided to certified participants.
resources.eligibility: Utah residents who are postpartum women up to one year after birth, meet the household-income guideline or are adjunctively eligible through Medicaid, SNAP, or TANF, and complete a WIC health/nutrition assessment. Non-breastfeeding postpartum certification is generally through six months; breastfeeding certification is through one year postpartum or until breastfeeding stops.
resources.how_to_connect: Call or text a local WIC clinic to apply and schedule a certification appointment. Bring proof of income, address, and identity, plus the infant or children being certified.
resources.availability_verified: Current state WIC pages indexed 2026-08-05 through 2026-09-05.

resources.services: Free, confidential guidance about the safety of medications and exposures during breastfeeding, as well as pregnancy.
resources.format_and_location: Phone and text; national service available to Utah residents.
resources.eligibility: People seeking information about medication or exposure safety during breastfeeding; no other eligibility requirement stated.
resources.how_to_connect: Call or text for guidance.
resources.availability_verified: Listed on the Utah DHHS maternal mental-health parent-resources page indexed 2026-10-05.

resources.services: Free, confidential mental-health support, resources, and referrals from trained counselors, 24 hours a day, every day. Available in English and Spanish.
resources.format_and_location: Call or text; nationwide service available to Utah residents.
resources.eligibility: Pregnant women, moms, and new parents; no insurance or other eligibility requirement is stated.
resources.how_to_connect: Call or text the hotline. Use your preferred relay service or dial 711, then the hotline number, for TTY access.
resources.availability_verified: Current HRSA page indexed 2026-10-03.

resources.services: Support and resources to help women heal emotionally after placing a baby for adoption.
resources.format_and_location: Not stated.
resources.eligibility: Women who have placed a baby for adoption; no other eligibility requirement stated.
resources.how_to_connect: Call or email for current services and availability.
resources.availability_verified: Listed on the Utah DHHS maternal mental-health parent-resources page indexed 2026-10-05.

resources.program: Food Pantry and Mobile Pantry Locator
resources.services: Connects Utah households with food pantries and mobile pantries. The online locator can be filtered by address, neighborhood, ZIP code, operating hours, and locations open today.
resources.format_and_location: Food assistance locations statewide; services and hours vary by site.
resources.cost: Food distributed through the Utah Food Bank's partner network is free of charge.
resources.eligibility: Varies by pantry or program. Confirm requirements and operating hours with the selected location before visiting.
resources.how_to_connect: Use the pantry locator to find a nearby location. Call 211 if help is needed finding food, housing, utilities, or health-care resources.
resources.availability_verified: Current Utah Food Bank pages indexed 2026-10-01 through 2026-10-05.

resources.program: SNAP, Financial, Medical, and Child Care Assistance
resources.services: State benefit application and case-management portal for SNAP food-purchasing assistance, financial assistance, Medicaid/medical assistance, and child-care assistance. The program also directs parents to Care About Childcare to locate providers.
resources.format_and_location: Online application and Utah employment centers.
resources.eligibility: Program-specific. The state determines eligibility for each benefit; SNAP is for eligible low- and no-income people, and child-care assistance supports families with qualifying work, employment-search, or other approved circumstances.
resources.how_to_connect: Apply online or contact Eligibility Services. Applicants with little or no money may be able to receive SNAP within seven days.
resources.availability_verified: Current Department of Workforce Services pages indexed 2026-09-05 through 2026-10-05.

resources.services: State database for locating childcare providers and reviewing provider profiles in Utah.
resources.format_and_location: Online statewide search.
resources.cost: No fee stated for using the search. Provider tuition or fees vary.
resources.eligibility: No eligibility requirement stated for searching the directory.
resources.how_to_connect: Use the state search portal to locate providers. For potential help paying for care, apply separately through the Department of Workforce Services child-care assistance program.
resources.availability_verified: Current state portal indexed 2026-10-03.

resources.program: Crisis and Respite Nurseries, Parenting Education, and Family Support
resources.services: Statewide network offering crisis and respite nursery care, parenting education, family-strengthening support, and services that vary by center. Some centers also offer therapy, counseling, or local referrals. The network reports 17 crisis and respite nurseries operating 24/7.
resources.format_and_location: Locations across Utah; services and hours differ by center.
resources.cost: Varies by center and service. Several crisis-nursery and parenting-education services are described as free.
resources.eligibility: Varies by center. The Family Support Center's crisis nurseries serve children ages 0–11 and state that they have no eligibility requirements; contact the local center to confirm availability and any local rules.
resources.how_to_connect: Find the nearest center through the statewide network, or call the after-hours Crisis Nursery line for the Salt Lake-area Family Support Center.
resources.availability_verified: Current Family Support Center pages indexed 2026-09-21 through 2026-10-03.

resources.services: Free research-based relationship education workshops and resources for individuals, couples, and families. Topics include communication, relationship skills, and family bonds; online and in-person options vary by course.
resources.format_and_location: Workshops throughout Utah and online options, depending on the course.
resources.eligibility: Individuals, couples, and families. Course-specific participation requirements and registration may apply.
resources.how_to_connect: Review available courses and register for a class that fits the mother's or family's needs.
resources.availability_verified: Current USU Extension pages indexed 2026-10-05.

resources.services: Free, confidential 24-hour support, resources, safety-planning help, and connections to local domestic-violence services. Support is available by call or text.
resources.format_and_location: Phone and text; statewide Utah service.
resources.eligibility: People experiencing domestic violence and their loved ones; no other eligibility requirement stated.
resources.how_to_connect: Call or text the LINKLine. If someone is in immediate danger, call 911.
resources.availability_verified: Current UDVC pages indexed 2026-10-03 through 2026-10-05.

resources.services: Confidential resource navigation and a searchable statewide directory connecting Utah residents to thousands of health, social, and government services, including food, housing, utilities, healthcare, transportation, childcare, and mental-health resources.
resources.format_and_location: Phone, text, online, and mobile app; statewide Utah service with language support.
resources.eligibility: No eligibility requirement stated for information and referral. Eligibility for referred programs varies.
resources.how_to_connect: Dial 211, text a ZIP code to the specialist line, or search online. Ask for postpartum, food, childcare, housing, relationship-safety, or mental-health resources as applicable.
resources.availability_verified: Current 211 Utah pages indexed 2026-10-03.

resources.organization: Utah Department of Health and Human Services
resources.services: Searchable statewide guide for free, low-cost, Medicaid-accepting, and Spanish-accessible services, including postpartum doula support, food and diapers, housing, transportation, legal support, childcare, healthcare, and mental-health resources.
resources.format_and_location: Online statewide directory; English and Spanish.
resources.eligibility: No eligibility requirement stated for using the guide. Eligibility for listed services varies.
resources.how_to_connect: Choose a category in the guide and contact the selected provider directly.
resources.availability_verified: Current Utah DHHS guide indexed 2026-08-05 and 2026-10-03.

resources.organization: Utah Department of Health and Human Services
resources.services: Free, voluntary parenting support during pregnancy and early childhood. A trained home visitor meets with families in a comfortable setting and helps build parenting confidence and connect families to services.
resources.format_and_location: Home or another comfortable setting; availability varies by participating local health department or nonprofit agency.
resources.eligibility: Pregnant women, parents, and families with young children. Specific local-program eligibility may vary.
resources.how_to_connect: Use the state program page to find parent resources or request local connection information.
resources.availability_verified: Current Utah DHHS page indexed 2026-10-05.

resources.services: Full Medicaid medical coverage for eligible women from the application date through pregnancy and 12 months after the birth of the child. Once eligible, coverage continues for the entire coverage period.
resources.format_and_location: Statewide Utah Medicaid benefit.
resources.eligibility: Pregnant women who meet Utah Medicaid eligibility requirements. Postpartum coverage applies for 12 months after birth once eligible.
resources.how_to_connect: Apply through the Utah Department of Workforce Services, or review the Utah Medicaid program page for details.
resources.availability_verified: Current Utah Medicaid pages indexed 2026-10-03.

resources.organization: Huntsman Mental Health Institute, University of Utah Health
resources.services: Structured, short-term perinatal and reproductive mental-health treatment with group therapy three days per week, weekly treatment reviews, and medication-management appointments as needed.
resources.format_and_location: Salt Lake City; Tuesday–Thursday, 10:00 a.m.–1:00 p.m.; 8–10 weeks. Rolling admission after an initial evaluation.
resources.cost: Not stated; contact the program about insurance and payment.
resources.eligibility: Adults age 18 or older whose mental health is affected by pregnancy, postpartum adjustment, childbirth, parenting, pregnancy loss, or related trauma. An initial evaluation determines whether the program is appropriate.
resources.how_to_connect: Call for an evaluation or enrollment information. Providers may also refer a patient by email.
resources.availability_verified: Current official program page indexed 2026-10-02.

resources.services: Provides diapers, wipes, hygiene products, clothing, and other essential items to Utah families experiencing financial hardship.
resources.format_and_location: Utah-based; check the Diaper Bank page for current distribution details and hours.
resources.cost: No charge stated for items provided.
resources.eligibility: Families experiencing financial hardship; specific Diaper Bank access requirements are not stated.
resources.how_to_connect: Visit the Diaper Bank page or contact the organization to confirm current hours, location, and access process.
resources.availability_verified: Current organization and Diaper Bank pages indexed 2026-09-30 through 2026-10-05.

resources.program: Free Civil Legal Help and Referral
resources.services: Free legal help for qualifying low-income Utahns in non-criminal cases. Areas include family problems, domestic-violence protective orders, housing, Medicaid and other public benefits, and employment-related matters. The organization may connect people it cannot directly assist with volunteer or pro bono attorneys.
resources.format_and_location: Online intake and statewide phone access; service availability varies by legal issue and eligibility.
resources.eligibility: Generally requires citizenship or lawful permanent-resident status and financial eligibility. The organization states an exception may apply when a case results from domestic violence. Case type and service capacity also affect eligibility.
resources.how_to_connect: Apply online or call to determine whether assistance is available.
resources.availability_verified: Current Utah Legal Services pages indexed 2026-09-29 through 2026-10-05.

resources.organization: La Leche League Utah and Idaho
resources.services: Education, information, support, and encouragement for parents who want to breastfeed or use human milk feeding. The organization provides a leader and group locator.
resources.format_and_location: Utah and Idaho; individual support and meeting availability vary by leader and group.
resources.cost: Not stated for local support. La Leche League USA states its meetings are free.
resources.eligibility: Parents seeking breastfeeding or human-milk feeding support; no other eligibility requirement stated.
resources.how_to_connect: Use the leader and group locator to identify current support. Confirm a local leader or meeting's availability before referring a mother.
resources.availability_verified: Current regional site indexed 2026-10-04. Local meeting availability must be confirmed through the locator.

resources.services: Statewide breastfeeding resource hub that directs families to lactation consultants, La Leche League Utah, WIC breastfeeding and nutrition services, and other feeding-support resources.
resources.format_and_location: Online statewide resource hub.
resources.cost: Free to use; costs for referred services vary.
resources.eligibility: No eligibility requirement stated for using the directory.
resources.how_to_connect: Use the resource page to find a lactation consultant or peer-support option that fits the mother's needs.
resources.availability_verified: Current Utah Breastfeeding Coalition pages indexed 2026-09-21 through 2026-10-02.

resources.services: Free, confidential 24/7 crisis support for people experiencing or concerned about a behavioral, mental, or emotional health crisis, including suicide prevention and mental-health intervention.
resources.format_and_location: Call or text; nationwide service available in Utah.
resources.eligibility: Anyone experiencing a crisis or worried about someone in crisis.
resources.how_to_connect: Call or text 988. Call 911 if there is immediate danger or an emergency requiring in-person response.
resources.availability_verified: Listed on the Utah DHHS maternal mental-health parent-resources page indexed 2026-10-05.
